messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: cleaning up Stan output
parts:
Currently Stan outputs an update every 10th of the run. That’s 40 outputs in a typical 4-chain run. 40 lines of output makes it impossible to read the console.

Here’s my proposal:

1. Just spit out two messages: one after 10% of warmup iterations giving estimated total time, another after 10% of the sampling iterations with an updated estimated time, since they can be faster than warmup.

2. Just print one pair of messages on the console, no matter how many chains are running. Simplest would be to just wait until all 4 (or however many) chains have sent out their 10% messages, then print the latest of these onto the console.

3. Also we should have a no-print option. We could have multiple verbose settings, but I’d like a default that is something like my suggestion above, also a no-print option, also maybe an option that prints out more, that I dunno.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] cleaning up Stan output
parts:
I like our current output. I wouldn't mind having an Andrew-mode
that does (1) for cases that only take a few seconds to run. Otherwise,
I want intermediate "pacifier" output to let me know it's still going.
When you're running something that takes 24 hours, getting one
message after 3 hours and another after 13 hours isn't so helpful,
especially when the time estimates will be super noisy.

Doing (2) presents technical challenges with interprocess
communication that are going to be a pain, if not impossible.

(3) we have, though I believe it may still produce some output.
This is something we need to fix, but I don't even know if there's
an issue for it.

- Bob

parts:

Regarding #1, perhaps we can have a default which does the printout after 10% and then decides what to do. If the first 10% took less than X minutes, it does my strategy. If it took more than X minutes, it does Bob’s strategy. We could for example set X=15. (Bob’s note below suggests that X should be something more than 1/60 and something less than 180.)

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] cleaning up Stan output
parts:
